sections.h2: Where is Belmont County, Ohio, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Belmont County sits on the eastern edge of Ohio, with the Ohio River running along its east line opposite West Virginia. Wikipedia lists 541.27 square miles of area, most of it low rolling hills cut by creeks such as Captina and McMahon. St. Clairsville is the county seat, and Martins Ferry is the largest city.

The county was created on September 7, 1801, and has kept its present boundaries since 1813. Coal, the National Road and the river trade shaped it early. Bellaire counted 15 glass factories by 1881 and was called the Glass City. Today the county is part of the Wheeling metropolitan area.

Census counts show 66,497 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 64,434 for 2025, a drop of 3.1 percent. About a quarter of residents are 65 or older, which matters later in this guide because the senior homestead credit is one of the main tax breaks here. Public high schools sit in Bellaire, Bridgeport, Martins Ferry, Saint Clairsville and Shadyside, and Buckeye Local and Union Local have high schools of their own.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Belmont County homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Belmont County shows a modest, owner-heavy market. Figures below cover 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $154,900.
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 73.6 percent, across 27,195 households.
  • Median gross rent: $793 a month.
  • Median household income: $57,017, with 15.1 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Mean commute: 25.1 minutes.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 2.

The county auditor's own site lists 76,512 parcels. Each parcel carries its own billing history, so a seller can ask the treasurer for the exact balance on a parcel number.

sections.h2: Which Belmont County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices in the courthouse at 101 West Main Street in St. Clairsville cover almost everything a seller needs. The auditor values property, the treasurer bills and collects, and the recorder files the deed.

  • Auditor. Sets values, takes board of revision complaints and endorses deeds. The main line is 740-699-2130, real estate is 740-699-2132, and the deed transfer desk is 740-699-2136. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Treasurer. Mails the bills and takes payment. Call 740-699-2145, Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Recorder. Files deeds and mortgages and, in the recorder's words, looks after more than 220 years of county land records. The office does not run title searches.

Ask the treasurer for the rate of taxation that applies to your taxing district, because school and village levies differ from one part of the county to another.

sections.h2: When are Belmont County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is billed twice a year, with bills going out in January and June. The treasurer's FAQ says the due dates generally land in the third week of February and the third week of July unless the bill says otherwise.

Belmont County tax calendar for 2025 taxes payable in 2026
ItemDate or rule
First-half bills mailedThird week of January 2026
First half dueFriday, February 20, 2026
Second-half bills mailedWeek of July 1, 2026
Second half dueFriday, July 24, 2026
Late penalty5 percent within ten days after the due date, then 10 percent
Valuation complaint windowJanuary 1 to March 31

Source: Belmont County Treasurer, treasurer FAQ and auditor timeline.

A postmark counts as timely, and the treasurer suggests carrying the envelope into the post office so it gets stamped. A secure drop box sits on the left side of the courthouse front stairs and is open only during the January and February and June and July collection periods. Cash does not go in the box.

Ohio bills taxes one year behind. A bill that arrives in 2026 is for tax year 2025, which is why a house sold in the spring can still produce a bill in the old owner's name.

sections.h2: What happens when a Belmont County tax payment is late?
sections.html:
The county adds a penalty first and interest later. Under Ohio Revised Code 323.121, a ten percent penalty attaches to an unpaid half, and interest on older delinquent tax runs at the rate set under section 5703.47.

The treasurer's FAQ is blunt on two points. A missing bill is no excuse, since the owner is responsible under section 323.13. A request to remit the penalty can still be filed when something outside the owner's control got in the way, such as hospitalization, a prolonged illness or the death of an immediate family member.

Owners who are behind should call 740-699-2145 and ask about payment options. The statute recognizes delinquent tax contracts, and while one stays in effect no ten percent penalty is added to the covered first-half taxes after the second-half collection period.

If back taxes go unpaid long enough, the parcel can reach tax foreclosure. The auditor's office has run forfeited land sales for parcels that failed to sell at foreclosure. The opening bid equals current taxes plus court costs, and the winning bidder pays the deed, conveyance and recording fees. Selling the house before that point keeps the proceeds with the owner.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Belmont County valuation?
sections.html:
File a complaint with the county auditor, who serves as secretary to the board of revision. Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 sets the deadline at March 31 of the following tax year or the close of first-half collection, whichever is later. The treasurer's FAQ gives March 31.

The board must give at least ten days' notice of the hearing. A mailed complaint is judged by its United States postmark, and a private meter mark does not count. Taxing bodies such as a school board can file their own complaints or counter-complaints, so the district may appear at the hearing.

Belmont County's latest reappraisal ran on this path:

  • January 2022: the Ohio Department of Taxation ordered the reappraisal for tax year 2024.
  • April 2022: data mailers went to every property with a dwelling.
  • Summer and fall 2024: informal reviews with owners.
  • October 2024: final values went to the state.
  • January 2025: bills with the new values were mailed, and the complaint window ran January 1 to March 31, 2025.

Ohio generally limits an owner to one complaint per interim period, with listed exceptions such as an improvement added to the property or a 15 percent swing in occupancy. Ask the auditor which year Belmont County sits in before filing.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks can a Belmont County owner claim?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the main one. The Ohio Department of Taxation lists a $29,700 reduction in market value for tax year 2026 for low-income seniors and disabled owners, and $59,400 for disabled veterans. The income ceiling printed for tax year 2026 is $41,000.

Applicants file with the county auditor by December 31 of the year they want the credit. A denial can be appealed to the board of revision on form DTE 106B within 60 days. The treasurer's site also carries the homestead application for seniors, disabled residents and surviving spouses.

The credit follows the owner and the home, so a buyer does not inherit it. That is why the deed paperwork asks about it, as the next section explains.

sections.h2: How is tax handled when a Belmont County house sells?
sections.html:
The auditor's endorsement is the first step on a deed. Under section 319.202, the buyer's side submits a statement of value, and that statement confirms the seller was asked whether the home's taxes carry a homestead or owner-occupancy reduction. If the answer is yes, a sworn statement with the estimated reduction goes with the deed.

Section 319.54(G)(3) sets the auditor's fee for the statement of value at one dollar, or ten cents per hundred dollars of value, whichever is greater, with listed exemptions such as transfers between spouses or between parent and child. Counties may add their own transfer tax of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars under section 322.02. Ask the deed transfer desk at 740-699-2136 for Belmont County's current conveyance rate.

The treasurer's FAQ tells sellers who still receive a bill after closing to check the closing documents and then call the title company, banker or agent. Unpaid tax that the closing statement never addressed can stay with the owner. Pay off or prorate the bill at the table.

faqs.q: Is the Belmont County second-half tax bill due in July?
faqs.a: Yes, the second half is generally due in the third week of July. For tax year 2025 the due date was Friday, July 24, 2026, and the first half was due Friday, February 20, 2026. Bills are mailed in January and June or early July, so check the date printed on yours.

faqs.q: Who values a house in Belmont County?
faqs.a: The county auditor values every parcel, and the auditor's office lists 76,512 of them. The treasurer only bills and collects. If you disagree with the value, the complaint goes to the auditor as secretary of the board of revision.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Belmont County?
faqs.a: The penalty is 5 percent when payment arrives within ten days after the due date and 10 percent after that on the unpaid current balance, per the treasurer's notice. The statute also adds interest on older delinquent tax. A penalty remission request is possible for circumstances beyond your control.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Belmont County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the treasurer at 740-699-2145 for the payoff figure and have the title company settle it at closing. A sale ahead of any tax foreclosure keeps the decision with you, where a forfeited land sale ends it.

faqs.q: Does the homestead credit transfer to the buyer of my Belmont County home?
faqs.a: No. The credit belongs to the qualifying owner who lives in the home. The deed paperwork asks the seller whether a reduction applies, and the buyer must apply on his or her own if eligible. Applications go to the county auditor by December 31.
